results.name: set_mean_variance
results.description: Variance across number sets (with >=18 responses) of the per-set mean yes rate; observed above null means sets differ in overall generalization breadth more than the digit-similarity model with a single intercept allows.
results.code:
# name: set_mean_variance
# description: Variance across number sets (with >=18 responses) of the per-set mean yes rate; observed above null means sets differ in overall generalization breadth more than the digit-similarity model with a single intercept allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df.groupby("number_set")["rating"].agg(["mean", "size"])
    g = g[g["size"] >= 18]
    return float(g["mean"].var(ddof=0)) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: item_mean_variance
results.description: Variance across (set, target) items of the item mean yes rate; observed above null means human judgments differ across items more sharply than the digit-similarity model predicts (model too flat / missing item-relevant features), below means the model over-discriminates.

results.name: inside_minus_outside_range
results.description: On 2-4 example sets, yes rate for targets strictly inside the examples' min-max range minus targets outside it; observed above null means people use interval/range-based generalization that the magnitude-blind digit model lacks, below null means they favour out-of-range targets more than predicted.
results.code:
# name: inside_minus_outside_range
# description: On 2-4 example sets, yes rate for targets strictly inside the examples' min-max range minus targets outside it; observed above null means people use interval/range-based generalization that the magnitude-blind digit model lacks, below null means they favour out-of-range targets more than predicted.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    inside = (n >= 2) & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    outside = (n >= 2) & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if inside.sum() == 0 or outside.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[inside].mean() - r[outside].mean())

results.name: opposite_parity_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets whose parity differs from every example (zero final-digit/parity similarity, the model's floor) on sets with >=2 examples; observed above null means people accept parity-violating targets more than the digit model's floor allows (parity/digit is not the operative dimension), below null means they reject them more sharply.
results.code:
# name: opposite_parity_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for targets whose parity differs from every example (zero final-digit/parity similarity, the model's floor) on sets with >=2 examples; observed above null means people accept parity-violating targets more than the digit model's floor allows (parity/digit is not the operative dimension), below null means they reject them more sharply.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    same_par = np.sum(valid & ((np.where(valid, ex, 0) % 2) == (t[:, None] % 2)), axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (same_par == 0)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0

results.name: trial_index_drift
results.description: Pearson correlation between trial_index and rating (yes); the model has no time dependence so the null is ~0, observed above null means participants say yes more as the session goes on, below means they become more conservative over trials.

results.name: math_rule_without_digit_match
results.description: Among targets sharing no final digit with any example on 2-4 example sets, yes rate for targets that share every non-parity arithmetic property common to all examples (mult of 3/4/5/10, power of 2, perfect square; set must have >=1 such property) minus yes rate for targets lacking all of them; observed above null means people generalize by mathematical rules that the final-digit model cannot see.
results.code:
# name: math_rule_without_digit_match
# description: Among targets sharing no final digit with any example on 2-4 example sets, yes rate for targets that share every non-parity arithmetic property common to all examples (mult of 3/4/5/10, power of 2, perfect square; set must have >=1 such property) minus yes rate for targets lacking all of them; observed above null means people generalize by mathematical rules that the final-digit model cannot see.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    exf = np.where(valid, ex, 1.0)
    p2 = np.array([1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64], dtype=float)
    sq = np.arange(1, 11, dtype=float) ** 2
    def props(x):
        return [x % 3 == 0, x % 4 == 0, x % 5 == 0, x % 10 == 0, np.isin(x, p2), np.isin(x, sq)]
    pe = props(exf)
    pt = props(t)
    shared = [np.all(np.where(valid, p, True), axis=1) for p in pe]
    nshared = np.sum(shared, axis=0)
    has_all = np.ones(len(t), bool)
    has_none = np.ones(len(t), bool)
    for s, q in zip(shared, pt):
        has_all &= (~s) | q
        has_none &= (~s) | (~q)
    digit_match = np.any(valid & ((exf % 10) == (t[:, None] % 10)), axis=1)
    base = (n >= 2) & (nshared >= 1) & (~digit_match)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a = base & has_all
    b = base & has_none
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: singleton_minus_multi_yes
results.description: Yes rate on 1-example sets minus yes rate on 3-4 example sets; observed above null means people generalize more broadly from one example and tighten with more examples (size principle) more than the averaged-similarity model predicts, below null means the reverse.

results.name: magnitude_proximity_residual_corr
results.description: Correlation between rating and -log(1 + distance from target to nearest example), after demeaning both within strata of identical final-digit/parity feature values (the model's only inputs); observed above null (~0) means people credit numerical closeness that the digit-only model ignores, below means they penalize it.
results.code:
# name: magnitude_proximity_residual_corr
# description: Correlation between rating and -log(1 + distance from target to nearest example), after demeaning both within strata of identical final-digit/parity feature values (the model's only inputs); observed above null (~0) means people credit numerical closeness that the digit-only model ignores, below means they penalize it.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ex = pd.DataFrame(sets.tolist(), index=df.index).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    same_dig = np.nansum((ex % 10) == (t[:, None] % 10), axis=1) / n
    same_par = np.nansum(((ex % 2) == (t[:, None] % 2)) & ((ex % 10) != (t[:, None] % 10)), axis=1) / n
    key = pd.Series(np.round(same_dig, 3).astype(str)) + "_" + pd.Series(np.round(same_par, 3).astype(str))
    prox = -np.log1p(d)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    tmp = pd.DataFrame({"k": key.values, "p": prox, "r": r})
    pr = tmp["p"] - tmp.groupby("k")["p"].transform("mean")
    rr = tmp["r"] - tmp.groupby("k")["r"].transform("mean")
    den = np.sqrt((pr ** 2).sum() * (rr ** 2).sum())
    return float((pr * rr).sum() / den) if den > 0 else 0.0
